# TLS Certificate Rotation

## Symptoms
- TLS errors on ingress/route; cert nearing expiry

## Diagnosis
1. Identify expiring certs (ingress, mTLS, webhooks).
2. cert-manager Certificate status if used.

## Remediation
- Issue replacement via cert-manager or PKI workflow.
- Rolling restart pods if hot-reload unsupported.

## Verification
- TLS handshake succeeds; ingress health checks pass.

# CNI Plugin Not Ready

## Symptoms
- Pod sandbox creation failed — CNI plugin not initialized
- Node NotReady with network unavailable

## Diagnosis
- oc get pods -n openshift-multus or kube-system — CNI pods
- Check node conditions NetworkUnavailable

## Remediation
- Restart CNI/daemonset pods on affected node
- Verify CNI config on node (/etc/cni/net.d)
- (OpenShift) Check openshift-sdn or OVN-Kubernetes operator health

## Verification
- New pods get IP addresses; node Ready

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/compute-storage-net/network-plugins/

# Connection Refused

## Symptoms
- TCP connection refused between pods or to service

## Diagnosis
1. App listening on declared containerPort?
2. NetworkPolicy blocking traffic?

## Remediation
- Fix bind address (0.0.0.0); open required ports in policy.

## Verification
- curl from client pod succeeds.

# DNS Resolution Failure

## Symptoms
- Apps fail resolving cluster.local or external hosts

## Diagnosis
1. CoreDNS/kube-dns pod health.
2. `oc run debug --image=busybox -- nslookup kubernetes.default`.

## Remediation
- Restart DNS pods; fix upstream forward config.
- OpenShift: check DNS operator and NetworkPolicy.

## Verification
- In-cluster and external DNS resolve from test pod.

# Empty EndpointSlice

## Symptoms
- Service has no ready endpoints; traffic blackholed

## Diagnosis
- oc get endpointslice -n <namespace> -l kubernetes.io/service-name=<svc>
- Verify pod labels match service selector and pods are Ready

## Remediation
- Fix selector or pod labels; fix failing readiness probes

## Verification
- EndpointSlice lists ready pod IPs

## Source
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/endpoint-slices/

# Ingress / Route 502 Bad Gateway

## Symptoms
- External users see 502; ingress cannot reach backends

## Diagnosis
1. Ingress controller logs; backend service endpoints.
2. OpenShift Route target port vs container port.

## Remediation
- Fix service port mapping or backend health.

## Verification
- HTTP check returns 200 from ingress URL.

# NetworkPolicy Troubleshooting

## Symptoms
- Connection timeouts between services; traffic unexpectedly blocked

## Diagnosis
1. Map source/destination pods and labels.
2. `oc get networkpolicy -n <ns>`; test with debug pod curl.

## Remediation
- Add minimal ingress/egress rules for required paths.

## Verification
- End-to-end connectivity restored.

# OpenShift Route Not Exposed

## Symptoms
- Route exists but traffic fails; edge termination issues

## Diagnosis
1. `oc get route` — host, tls, targetPort.
2. Ingress controller / router pod health.

## Remediation
- Fix route spec; ensure Service exposes correct port.

## Verification
- Route URL returns expected response.

# Service Has No Endpoints

## Symptoms
- Service exists but no endpoints; 503 from ingress

## Diagnosis
1. Selector labels match pod labels?
2. Are backend pods Ready?

## Remediation
- Fix selector or pod labels; fix failing readiness probes.

## Verification
- `oc get endpoints` shows ready addresses.

# TLS Handshake Failure

## Symptoms
- x509 or cipher mismatch errors

## Diagnosis
1. Compare cert SANs to hostname; check intermediate chain.

## Remediation
- Reissue cert with correct SAN; update trust store.

## Verification
- openssl s_client connects without verify errors.
